open_points.subject: time source for settling checks
open_points.text: A file is taken only after it has been unchanged for two minutes
open_points.question: What time source is compared with the file modification time to decide that two minutes have elapsed?
options: A UTC wall clock supplied to the scan
A monotonic clock combined with a captured filesystem timestamp
An ambient system clock read by the scanner
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected UTC wall clock because filesystem modification times are wall-clock instants.

witness.initial: A file's modification time is 12:00 UTC and the system wall clock is adjusted backward while the service remains running.
events: The owner starts a scan after two monotonic minutes have elapsed but while the wall clock reads 11:59.
The deliverer evaluates whether the file is settled.
outcomes: The file is ready because two monotonic minutes elapsed.
The file remains settling because the wall-clock difference is negative.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees ready versus settling.

open_points.subject: PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which authority supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at`?
options: A clock port passed to the mark operation or service
A datetime parameter supplied by the calling flow
A declared authority module
An ambient system-clock call inside the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a clock port owned by the deliverer and injected into the marking service.

open_points.subject: photo and mark datetime representation
open_points.text: with the moment the photo was taken as UTC without an offset
open_points.question: Does “UTC without an offset” mean a timezone-naive UTC `datetime`, an aware UTC `datetime` whose serialized form omits the offset, or a string, and must `marked_at` use the same representation?
options: Timezone-naive UTC datetime in memory and serialization
Timezone-aware UTC datetime in memory, serialized without an offset
A canonical UTC string without an offset
Different representations for photo dates and marked_at
open_points.default_guess: Use timezone-naive UTC `datetime` values consistently because the models declare `datetime` and explicitly say without an offset.

witness.initial: An EXIF timestamp denotes 10:00 UTC and a mark is created at 12:00 UTC.
events: The calling flow marks the publication.
The values are persisted and later returned.
outcomes: The service stores naive datetimes `10:00` and `12:00`.
The service stores aware UTC datetimes and merely strips offsets when serializing.
witness.observer: Persistence and API consumers see different datetime values or encodings.

open_points.subject: camera-record instant
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: Which camera timestamp field is authoritative, how is a camera time with no zone interpreted as a UTC instant, and what makes a camera record unusable so that modification time is used?
options: Use DateTimeOriginal and interpret an absent zone as UTC
Use DateTimeOriginal with its offset and reject or fall back when the offset is absent
Use a fixed deployment timezone for zone-less camera times
Use another ordered list of EXIF timestamp fields
open_points.default_guess: Use DateTimeOriginal with an explicit EXIF offset; if either is absent or invalid, fall back to file modification time.

witness.initial: A photo has EXIF DateTimeOriginal `2026:07:01 10:00:00` with no offset and a file modification time of 08:15 UTC.
events: The owner places the file in the photo folder.
outcomes: The photo date is treated as 10:00 UTC.
The EXIF value is unusable and the photo date becomes 08:15 UTC.
witness.observer: The Portal and owner see a different photo date.

open_points.subject: number of time readings per operation
open_points.text: A file is taken only after it has been unchanged for two minutes
open_points.question: How many readings of the decided time source does one scan, placement, or mark take, and is one captured instant shared by every time-dependent decision and write in that operation?
options: Exactly one clock reading per operation
One reading per file or comparison
Separate readings for comparisons and fresh timestamps
open_points.default_guess: Capture exactly one instant at the start of each operation and reuse it throughout that operation.

witness.initial: Two files have identical modification times and the two-minute boundary occurs while a scan is iterating them.
events: The calling flow starts one scan just before the boundary.
The deliverer evaluates the first file and then the second.
outcomes: Both files are settling because the scan uses one captured instant.
The first file is settling and the second is ready because the clock is read per file.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees different observations from the same scan.

open_points.subject: unreadable ObjectConnection
open_points.text: A record that cannot be read or breaks rule 7 refuses the operation with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: Exactly which failures mean that a record “cannot be read”: absence, permission or I/O failure, invalid encoding, parse/schema failure, unsupported version, or a transient/partial concurrent write?
options: Every storage, decoding, and validation failure after locating a record
Only filesystem I/O and permission failures
Only failures to deserialize an otherwise located record
A specified closed list of failures
open_points.default_guess: Treat every failure to load and validate a located record as unreadable, while a definitely absent record remains `unknown_project`.

open_points.subject: connection reload boundary
open_points.text: The service reads the connection record at each scan, placement and mark, so a change applies from the next operation without a restart.
open_points.question: When is the “next operation” determined for concurrent or queued requests, and must the connection be read exactly once into an immutable snapshot before any operation effects?
options: At request admission, with one immutable snapshot
When execution begins, after waiting for any operation lock
Immediately before the first folder or persistence effect
Repeatedly during the operation
open_points.default_guess: Read and validate one immutable snapshot after acquiring the operation's lock and before any folder or persistence effect.

witness.initial: A placement request is accepted but waits before accessing the source; its connection is confirmed.
events: The calling flow sends the placement request.
The agent clears `assignment_confirmed` while the request is waiting.
outcomes: The placement succeeds because it was the operation already admitted before the change.
The placement is refused because execution and the connection read occur after the change.
witness.observer: The calling flow and owner see whether a photo was placed.

open_points.subject: connection refusal precedence
open_points.text: An operation on a project with no connection is refused with `unknown_project`, and one with an unconfirmed connection with `connection_not_confirmed`. This is decided by the service, not by the caller. The service reads the connection record at each scan, placement and mark, so a change applies from the next operation without a restart. A record that cannot be read or breaks rule 7 refuses the operation with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: Which refusal wins when a located record is both unconfirmed and invalid under rule 7, or cannot be decoded well enough to determine its project or confirmation?
options: Unreadable or rule-7-invalid takes precedence over confirmation
Unconfirmed takes precedence whenever that field can be read
Apply a specified validation order and return its first failure
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate first, locate and fully load the record next, validate rule 7 next, and check confirmation last; therefore `folder_unavailable` wins over `connection_not_confirmed`.

witness.initial: A project's record has `assignment_confirmed` false and a photo subfolder containing `..`.
events: The calling flow invokes scan with the correct token.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different refusal code.

open_points.subject: rule 7 validation during mark
open_points.text: A record that cannot be read or breaks rule 7 refuses the operation with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: For a mark operation, does “breaks rule 7” include the live resolved-photo-folder requirement that rule 7 states only for scan and placement, or only the record's non-empty relative-path constraints?
options: Mark applies every lexical and live filesystem check in rule 7
Mark applies only rule 7's record-shape checks
Mark merely requires a readable confirmed connection because it does not access a folder
open_points.default_guess: For mark, apply the record-shape checks but not live photo-folder resolution, because rule 7 explicitly limits that filesystem check to scan and placement.

witness.initial: A confirmed connection has valid relative subfolders, but its photo-folder symlink has been changed to resolve outside the root after placement.
events: The calling flow publishes the already placed photo in the Portal.
The calling flow sends mark with the returned `photo_id`.
outcomes: Mark is refused with `folder_unavailable` because the live resolved folder breaks rule 7.
Mark succeeds because mark does not perform the scan-and-placement folder check.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees whether the publication mark is recorded.

open_points.subject: resolved folder containment
open_points.text: On each scan and placement the photo folder must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root, otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: Must containment remain true while files are accessed, and what mechanism prevents a symlink or mount change between the resolution check and the later read?
options: Containment is checked once and the later path lookup may race
The operation uses directory handles or equivalent traversal that preserves containment
Containment is rechecked immediately before every file access
open_points.default_guess: Use root-relative directory handles with no-follow traversal so the checked containment remains true through use.

witness.initial: The photo folder is a symlink resolving below the root when placement begins.
events: The service resolves and validates the photo folder.
Another local actor retargets the symlink outside the root.
The service opens the requested source file.
outcomes: The placement reads the outside file because only the earlier resolution was checked.
The placement is refused or remains confined because the validated directory handle is used.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether content from outside the object root is placed.

open_points.subject: INV-10 live-confirmation test
open_points.text: a confirmation cleared while the service runs stops the next operation (`test_a_cleared_confirmation_stops_the_running_service`)
open_points.question: Must this test demonstrate the live reload and absence of effects for scan, placement, and mark separately, and must it assert `connection_not_confirmed` rather than only that an operation did not deliver?
options: Exercise all three operations and assert the exact refusal plus no effects
Exercise one representative operation and rely on the earlier unconfirmed-connection test for the others
Assert only that no delivery effect occurs
open_points.default_guess: Exercise scan, placement, and mark after a runtime clear, asserting `connection_not_confirmed` and no folder, placement, or mark effects.

open_points.subject: INV-10 unreadable-record test
open_points.question: Which operations and unreadability cases must the check exercise, and must it assert `folder_unavailable`, no scanning, no placement, no mark, and no partial writes?
options: Cover scan, placement, and mark for every specified unreadability class and assert exact refusal and no effects
Cover one representative operation and one unreadability case
Assert only absence of a delivered photo
open_points.default_guess: Cover scan, placement, and mark for a representative storage failure and a malformed record, asserting `folder_unavailable` and no observable side effects.

open_points.subject: formal invariant for invalid or unreadable connections
open_points.text: A record that cannot be read or breaks rule 7 refuses the operation with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: Is this new safety requirement part of INV-10 or a new formal invariant, and which Required tests item states exactly what must be shown for unreadable records and every applicable rule-7 failure?
options: Extend INV-10 to cover unreadable and invalid connections and make its tests explicit
Create a separate formal invariant with its own Required tests item
Treat it only as a normative behavior with no formal invariant
open_points.default_guess: Extend INV-10 to say that no scan, placement, or mark effect occurs unless the connection is readable, valid for that operation, and confirmed, then bind explicit tests to each condition.

open_points.subject: A10 files_artifacts category
open_points.text: - files_artifacts: APPLICABLE; references: A1, A2, A6, A8; affected: M02, M03, M04, source folders, Portal binary store
open_points.question: Must this category now reference A5 and cover unreadable connection records, resolved-root containment, and runtime folder-link changes introduced by A5?
options: Add A5 and the connection record/path boundary to this category
Place the new A5 concerns in another explicitly named category
State why A5's new file and path rules do not affect this category
open_points.default_guess: Add A5 and ObjectConnection storage plus resolved-root containment to `files_artifacts`.

open_points.subject: A10 concurrency category
open_points.text: - concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A3, A4, A6; affected: M04, M07
open_points.question: Must the concurrency outcome now reference A5 and M01 because a connection can change while the running service is admitting or executing scan, placement, and mark operations?
options: Add A5 and M01 and decide the read/snapshot boundary
State that connection updates and operations are serialized elsewhere and reference that decision
State why the new live-reload behavior creates no concurrency concern
open_points.default_guess: Add A5 and M01 and require one validated connection snapshot after acquiring the operation lock.

open_points.subject: A5 refusal code
open_points.text: A record that cannot be read or breaks rule 7 refuses the operation with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: Make `folder_unavailable` a member of a models enumeration used as the refusal-code type, or give it another applicable one of the three stated paths to generated code instead of leaving the generated implementation to obtain the literal from prose.
